sections.h2: Quickest ways to sell in Glen Ellyn
sections.html:
Speed in Glen Ellyn usually comes from an as-is purchase by a buyer with no loan to approve, although a well-prepared listing can also hit a fixed date. What slows most closings is the village paperwork: the transfer stamp, the clearwater inspection and the final water reading.

  • An agent listing suits a house in good shape when you want to see how high the price can go.
  • Sell privately if you are comfortable handling contracts and disclosures on your own.
  • A cash purchase as-is fits a house with deferred repairs, an estate behind it, or a closing date that cannot move.

Glen Ellyn is a village in DuPage County about 24 miles due west of downtown Chicago, in Milton Township. Train access, school boundaries and basement drainage are the topics to prepare before you talk to buyers.

Glen Ellyn is a high-value suburb where most residents own. Population is 28,750, and the village has 10,698 households.

Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $544,000, and owners hold 78.3 percent of the housing. Median gross rent is $1,433 and median household income is $140,938.

The average trip to work takes 29.1 minutes, which is worth reading alongside the train and expressway access described below. Much of the housing is older, since the village dates to the 1800s and the railroad reached it in 1849.

School district is the first fact to confirm for any Glen Ellyn address. Primary schools are part of Glen Ellyn School District 41 and Community Consolidated School District 89, and high school students attend Glenbard Township High School District 87.

Elementary schools in the village include Abraham Lincoln, Arbor View, Benjamin Franklin, Churchill, Forest Glen, Park View and Westfield, and Glen Crest Middle School and Hadley Junior High serve older grades. Confirm which school serves your address with the district, since district boundaries do not follow village lines everywhere.

The Metra Union Pacific West Line stops at the Glen Ellyn station at 551 Crescent Boulevard, about 22.4 miles from Ogilvie Transportation Center. Pace routes 714, 715 and 301 run along Roosevelt Road, and Roosevelt Road also leads to Interstate 355 at the east end of the village. The Glen Ellyn Park District maintains 30 parks and two lakes, and the Illinois Prairie Path bike trail runs through the village.

The Village of Glen Ellyn charges a real estate transfer stamp of $3 for each $1,000 of property sales price, and the home seller pays it. The stamp is required to record the deed, and the village will not issue it until every inspection is passed and every fee is paid.

The clearwater inspection comes from Village Code 3-42-15. It is required any time a stamp is needed, including a sale, a title transfer, putting a deed into a trust or a refinance, and it applies to exempt transactions too. The inspector checks whether the building has a sump pump and whether the pump is illegally tied into the sanitary sewer.

sections.h2: Why the village checks sump pumps
sections.html:
Rainwater in the sanitary system can overload it during a major storm and push sewage back into homes. Village Code 7-9-25 bars clearwater from sanitary sewers, and Code 8-1-10 bars directing sump pump, gutter or similar discharge into the public right-of-way.

If the inspector finds a problem, fix it before closing. Public Works can explain acceptable options, which may include moving the discharge point or connecting to the storm sewer. Book the inspection early, since a failed result means a repair and a second visit before the stamp can be issued.

Some sellers may qualify for a refund of the transfer tax. The eligibility rules are on the village's refund application, so ask the village before assuming one applies.

Permit work in Glen Ellyn goes through the village's online permit system, and open work can complicate a sale. The Building Division reviews plans, issues permits, inspects construction and enforces the building, property maintenance, fire and zoning codes.

Applications are signed electronically with the owner's authorization, and supporting documents such as plans, a plat of survey and contracts are uploaded with them. Construction plans must be prepared and stamped by an Illinois registered design professional. Fees depend on the project type and construction cost, and refundable deposits cover possible damage to public property. All contractors must meet the license and insurance requirements in Village Code Section 4-1-11, and a contractor working in violation can be cited or have a stop work order issued.

  • Locate permit records and final inspection sign-offs for decks, additions and finished basements.
  • Ask Public Works about drainage if your lot has a history of standing water.
  • Keep a copy of your plat of survey, since many permit and closing steps ask for it.

Selling as-is to a cash buyer puts the cleanup of open permits on the buyer, as long as the contract spells out who takes on what.

Glen Ellyn sits in Milton Township, and DuPage County sends a single yearly bill with two coupons. They come due June 1 and September 1, and the U.S. postmark decides whether a payment is late. Late payments add 1.5 percent a month.

Valuation questions start at the township assessor, who sets the first assessed value at one-third of fair market value under state law. An owner who disagrees files with the DuPage County Board of Review within 30 days after the township roll is published, backed by three or more comparable properties. Decisions typically arrive the next March, and the next level is the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board.

New owners should contact the township assessor after moving in, because the residential exemption requires that you live in the home by January 1 of the tax year. For parcel questions, call the DuPage Supervisor of Assessments at 630-407-5858 or the Treasurer at 630-407-5900. Your closing agent prorates the bill at settlement, so ask the title company how the current year is being split.

faqs.q: Who pays the Glen Ellyn transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The home seller pays it. The rate is $3 for each $1,000 of sales price, and the stamp is issued only after the clearwater inspection is passed and all fees are paid.

faqs.q: What is a clearwater inspection in Glen Ellyn?
faqs.a: It is a village check for a sump pump and for any illegal sump connection to the sanitary sewer. Village Code 3-42-15 requires it when a transfer stamp is needed, and you schedule it with Public Works at 630-469-6756.

faqs.q: How do I schedule the final water reading in Glen Ellyn?
faqs.a: Call the Utility Billing Department at 630-547-5235 after you complete the online transfer stamp application. The reading and the clearwater inspection both come before the stamp.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Glen Ellyn house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, apart from anything required for the stamp, such as correcting an illegal clearwater connection. Cosmetic and mechanical repairs are negotiable in an as-is sale and are priced into the offer.

faqs.q: When are DuPage County property taxes due?
faqs.a: In two installments, June 1 and September 1. The coupons on your bill show the exact dates each year, and late payments add 1.5 percent a month.
